subject: Monitor v2: measure whether reload-per-session-switch is too coarse
description:
v2 switches sessions by reloading the shell, which was the DECIDED tradeoff on 2026-08-27:
`export.js` is one IIFE with ~78 module-level state vars, listeners on document/window and no
teardown, so a reload is what currently disposes of that state for free. The alternative is an
explicit init(container)/destroy() contract inside the html crate.

The decision was "reload first, revisit if it proves too coarse". Nobody has measured whether
it is. This task is the measurement plus the verdict, not the rewrite.

Definition of done: a number for switch latency on a large session (say >100 MB) on this
machine, a judgement recorded here, and either a follow-up task for the teardown contract or a
note closing the question. Background: design/monitor-v2.md.

metadata.deferred_reason: rides the held UX work; no signal yet that the reload hurts
